title: Chinese desserts in Zhangjiajie
text: Chinese sweets differ from Western desserts: less sugar, more texture and natural flavors. Must-try: Tangyuan (rice balls in syrup), lily in jelly, cold mung bean soup in summer, rice flour pastries and Tujia flower cakes. Luckin Coffee chain offers modern desserts for 15-25 yuan.

title: Street food of Zhangjiajie
text: The best spots are Wulizhou Bridge night market, Pipa Street in the city and the area by the north park gate. Try Choudofu (stinky tofu), Chuanr (skewers), noodles (10-15 yuan), steamed baozi, egg pancakes (jianbing) and sugared fruit on sticks. 50-80 yuan fills you up.

title: Tujia cuisine - authentic mountain flavors
text: The Tujia are indigenous to Zhangjiajie and their cuisine differs from Hunanese - less spicy, more smoked and fermented. Signature dishes: La Rou (smoked pork aged 3-6 months), Sanxiaguo (three ingredients in one pot), sweet rice wine, sugar-crusted fish and nut tea.

title: Hunan cuisine - fire in the mouth
text: Zhangjiajie sits in Hunan, home to one of China's Eight Great Cuisines. Unlike Sichuan's numbing ma la, Hunan heat is pure chili and sourness. Must-try: Duojiao Yutou (chili fish head), smoked pork with peppers, sour duck and bird's-eye chili chicken.

title: Hidden trails of the park (no crowds)
text: Main routes get packed in season, but alternatives exist: the 2-hour Yangjiajie trail between Yuanjiajie and Tianzi, the upper parallel Golden Whip path, remote Laowuchang, the Tujia villages inside the park and evening walks after 17:00 when the tour groups leave.
